core.title: Migrate legacy artifact names to theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant
core.given: A plan artifact, an artifact manifest or an acceptance artifact uses a legacy artifact name (no theme prefix, or dots for hierarchy).
core.when: The planner migrates that name to the current scheme.
core.then: Rewrite it as theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant — assign a theme, colons between hierarchy levels, dots only before variants — and realign every carrier that carries it: the artifact manifest, the acceptance artifacts, the URNs, the contract file locations and the identity fields, the stack's concrete manifest, acceptance-artifact, URN and identity-field carriers being identified through the profile's registry, artifact-kind and URN-grammar bindings.
prefer: Steps in order: identify names -> determine theme -> identify hierarchy -> separate hierarchy from variants -> update manifests -> update acceptance artifacts -> update URNs -> reorganize contract file locations -> update identity fields; the order is part of the procedure itself, not derived from any profile list, and the profile binds the manifest, acceptance-artifact, URN and identity-field slots to this stack's concrete carriers.

Illustrative template shapes only, not a mandatory mapping table: a legacy name gains a theme; a dotted hierarchy becomes colon-separated; a dot survives only before a variant — any structurally valid migrated name satisfies the scheme.
avoid: Renaming only the name while any carrier — manifest, acceptance artifact, URN, contract layout or identity field — keeps the old one.
Dots between hierarchy levels, or a colon before a variant.
core.why: Piecemeal migration leaves URNs, manifests and contract identity fields pointing at different identities; one form with colons for hierarchy and dots for variants keeps them consistent.
evidence: Each migrated name has a theme prefix, colons only between hierarchy levels and dots only before variants.
No carrier — manifest, acceptance artifact, URN, contract path or identity field — still references the legacy name.
Contract files are reorganized to match the new hierarchy and their identity fields are updated consistently with the migrated identity.
verification: Needs two observers that the reference realization marks needs_new_observer: a detector that recognises legacy-shape names (no theme prefix, or dots between hierarchy levels), and a diff-level observer that sees such a name being rewritten in names, URNs and identity-field values.

The check validates each migrated name structurally — theme prefix, colons only between hierarchy levels, dots only before variants; the realization's reference mappings are illustrative examples, not a conformance table, so a different structurally valid migrated name is acceptable.

The check also verifies that no carrier still references the legacy name — across the artifact manifest, the acceptance artifacts, the URNs, the contract file locations and the identity fields; the stack's concrete manifest, acceptance-artifact, URN and identity-field carriers are identified through the profile's registry, artifact-kind and URN-grammar bindings, while the contract tree's own layout is stack data that this rule does not further specify.
Task-keyword and file-kind cues are contextual only and never raise a finding by themselves; a finding requires an actual legacy name being migrated.
A finding may cite individual steps of the ordered migration procedure; the step term and its enumeration are realization vocabulary.

values: legacy artifact name in the pre-scheme shape (no theme prefix, or dots between hierarchy levels)
legacy name rewritten to the current scheme in names, URNs and identity-field values

fires: A plan-artifact or product-slice task migrates a legacy artifact name (no theme prefix, or dots for hierarchy) to theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant.

A planner migrates a legacy artifact name and must update every carrier that carries it — the artifact manifest, the acceptance artifacts, the URNs, the contract file locations and the identity fields.
A legacy name with no theme prefix is found while authoring a new product slice or acceptance artifact and is to be migrated.
doesNotFire: Authoring a brand-new artifact name with no legacy predecessor (the naming-pattern rule governs that).
Renaming an artifact whose name is already in theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant form (an ordinary rename, not a migration from the legacy shape).
Editing a contract or manifest whose names are already in the current form and are not being renamed.
A task that merely mentions migration keywords or touches manifests, acceptance files or contracts without any legacy name being migrated.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kind of the acceptance artifacts that carry artifact names and must be realigned when a name migrates.

The stack's artifact-manifest carrier: the registry/index file that enumerates one product slice's artifacts and carries their names, so that a migration finds and realigns it; the sidecar names this registry but states no location for it.
The identity field by which a contract schema declares its identity; the migrated name must be written into it.
The shape by which files and artifacts reference an artifact by URN, so that every URN carrying the legacy name is found and rewritten.

neutralityNotes: The core keeps the artifact-naming scheme itself — theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant, colons for hierarchy, dots for variants, and the legacy/current scheme-version labels — because that is convention content, not stack machinery; the legacy shape is always defined structurally (no theme prefix, or dots between hierarchy levels). No stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path is named. Per the round-3 fixes, the carrier inventory binds only where the Bun sidecar actually supplies data of the documented kind: the acceptance-artifact carrier binds as an artifact kind under a role key (roles.acceptance_test.kinds = feature_file); the wagon manifest binds as the stack's product-slice artifact registry under layout.registries (layout.registries#wagon_manifest = wagon manifest) — it is an index file enumerating a slice's artifacts and carrying their names, and bun.json names it without stating any location, so no layout.locations entry is claimed; the $id contract identity field and the URN reference shapes bind under urn.grammar (urn.grammar#identity_fields, urn.grammar#reference_shapes). Contract file reorganization remains wholly core content: bun.json states it as the migration obligation, not as contract-tree layout data, so no layout.contract_paths requirement is recorded and the contract tree's layout is treated as stack data this rule does not further specify. No new keys were proposed. The nine-step migration order is core content in prefer[0] and is not derived from any profile list ordering. The legacy-to-current reference mappings remain strictly illustrative: the core neither requires reusing them nor validates against them as a table — verification checks naming structure and carrier consistency only, so a different structurally valid migrated name passes. What stayed realization-side: the concrete legacy reference mappings (Bun-corpus names), the finding/change/term ids of this rule's observers, and the concrete carrier names themselves (wagon manifest, feature file, $id), which reach the core only through the profile bindings or stay in the delivered reference example. 'Product slice', 'contract schema' and 'identity field' are ATDD-concept-level terms that each stack binds via the profile.
